newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile Quebrada Blanca copper miners go on strike.
newsitem.headline: Chile Quebrada Blanca copper miners go on strike.

text.p: Workers at Chile's Quebrada Blanca copper mine rejected the company's final pay offer at an assembly Wednesday and have gone on strike, said union president Nelson Fuentes.
"The miners are on strike and the pit is paralyzed," Fuentes told Reuters by telephone from the union offices in Iquique.
He said union officials had held talks with management until dawn in a bid to avert a walk-out by over 300 unionized miners who represent most of the workforce.
Quebrada Blanca raised its pay offer to a nine percent rise in real terms, but this was still far below the union's demand for an 18 percent increase, he said.
With annual production of 75,000 tonnes of cathodes, Quebrada Blanca is one of Chile's smaller copper mines.
The walkout is the latest sign of labor unrest in Chile's all-important copper mining industry which has been hit by a rash of strikes recently.
A small group of miners at the huge Escondida pit began an indefinite stoppage nearly two weeks ago after collective wage talks broke down.
